title: Long UUP — Warsh Hawkish Rate Regime; DXY Holding $100; May PCE Catalyst June 25
entry: Enter $27.20–27.80 (UUP at ~$27.34 corresponding to DXY 100.15 on June 18 close). Scale: 60% initial at current levels on the Juneteenth holiday or Monday June 22 open; 40% add if DXY closes above 100.50 on Monday June 22 session (confirming the rate premium is sustaining into the first post-Juneteenth session). Do NOT add above $28.00 — at that DXY level (~104) the near-term move is largely captured. Reduce the position by 50% if DXY closes below 99.00 at any point (the BUY upgrade is firing and this hedge becomes a drag); exit fully if DXY closes below 98.50 on two consecutive sessions.
stop_loss: $26.50 daily close (~3.0% below $27.34 entry) — implies DXY has broken decisively below 99.00, the BUY upgrade regime condition is met, and the macro framework has shifted to risk-on. At this level, the Iran deal disinflation has finally overwhelmed the Warsh rate premium in FX markets. This is the exact scenario in which the long equity positions (NVDA add, GOOGL, META) activate — the UUP stop and the equity adds are designed to be simultaneous events that net-hedge the portfolio transition from HOLD to BUY.
targets: $28.20 — May PCE June 25 prints ≥4.1% YoY (Wells Fargo baseline estimate); Warsh hawkish signals reinforced; 30Y approaches 5.00% trigger; DXY at ~102.5; +3.1% from $27.34 entry
$29.00 — Warsh signals September 2026 rate hike at June FOMC minutes release (July); DXY at ~106; full Warsh hike cycle pricing accelerates; +6.1%

$30.50 — blue sky: PCE sustained above 4.0% through Q3 2026; Warsh raises rates in September AND December 2026; DXY enters 111–114 zone; dollar reaches the level that historically causes EM stress and Fed-pivot-demand from the market; +11.6%
catalyst: The June 18 DXY close at 100.15 — after a confirmed Iran ceasefire signing, a 5% Brent crude collapse, and a +1.91% Nasdaq session — is the definitive empirical signal that the Warsh rate premium is dominating geopolitical and commodity disinflation in FX markets. Every structural headwind that should weaken the dollar materialized on June 17–18 (oil collapsing, Iran deal removing safe-haven bid, equities rallying reducing flight-to-quality demand for USD), and DXY closed essentially flat. The May PCE data on June 25 (Wells Fargo estimate: core PCE +0.3% MoM, 3.4% YoY) is the next inflection point: a print at or above 4.0% YoY would reinforce Warsh's nine hike dots and drive DXY above 102.
thesis:
The June 18 DXY close at 100.15 constitutes a stress test of the geopolitical disinflation thesis, and DXY passed with flying colors — meaning the dollar held. When a confirmed, signed ceasefire removes the conflict-era risk premium from energy markets simultaneously with a 5% oil price decline, and the dollar still does not move below 100, the market is telling you something explicit: the Warsh rate-hike path (nine dots, 3.8% median, no forward guidance) is a rate premium that operates independently of the geopolitical channel. This is the most important diagnostic in the current macro regime. The old UUP long (from May 28) was positioned on a combined geopolitical safe-haven + PCE catalyst thesis; that position was correctly marked thesis-broken when the Iran deal removed the safe-haven component. This new UUP position is solely a rate-premium expression — the thesis is Warsh's explicit rate path, not geopolitical uncertainty.

UUP (Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund) tracks DXY futures contracts. At $27.34, UUP is near the lower end of its 50-day range ($27.04–$28.65), reflecting a DXY that has been in a tight band around 99–101 since the FOMC. The May PCE data on June 25 is the catalyst with the highest asymmetry. If core PCE prints at 3.4% YoY (Wells Fargo baseline), it confirms the Warsh dot trajectory and provides no relief from the current HOLD ceiling — DXY stays near 100, UUP near $27.50. If core PCE prints at 4.0%+ (tail risk scenario given May retail sales +0.9% and shelter inflation persistence), the 30Y would breach 5.00% in the same session, VIX would spike, and DXY would accelerate to 102–104, taking UUP to $28.00–$28.50 within the PCE session.

This position is complementary to TBT, not duplicative. TBT (2× inverse TLT) captures the 30Y yield expression of Warsh hawkishness — it gains when 30Y yields rise. UUP captures the FX (dollar index) expression. The two instruments diverge in a stagflation scenario: if the US economy slows (weak GDP, falling consumer confidence) while the Fed maintains hawkish rhetoric, the yield curve flattens — TBT could underperform as the long end is bid — but UUP would still hold (or rally) because the Fed's rate premium sustains the dollar regardless of growth trajectory. Holding both provides regime coverage: under HOLD maintained (most likely), both TBT and UUP gain slowly; under STEP_ASIDE (DXY spike, VIX spike), both accelerate; under BUY upgrade (DXY breaks 99.00), UUP stop is triggered simultaneously with the equity adds, creating a natural portfolio rebalance.

The invalidation is clean and precisely calibrated. DXY breaking below 99.00 on a daily close is the ONLY event that simultaneously: (1) triggers the UUP stop; (2) fires the BUY upgrade for equities; (3) removes the Warsh rate premium thesis. This makes the UUP stop a portfolio transition mechanism rather than a simple loss event. In the BUY upgrade scenario, the 3% UUP position absorbs a ~3% loss ($26.50 stop vs. $27.34 entry) while the portfolio adds NVDA at $205–215, GOOGL at $368–375, and MU scaling — more than offsetting the UUP loss if those longs work. The stop and the equity activations are designed as a simultaneous rebalancing event.
bull_case: Monday June 22 DXY opens above 100.5 as Juneteenth holiday appetite for Iran-deal disinflation fades. May PCE June 25 prints core at 3.7%+ YoY — at or above the Wells Fargo estimate of 3.4%. 30Y approaches 5.00% on the PCE session; Warsh dot plot is reinforced. DXY closes above 101.5 on June 25; UUP rallies to $28.00–$28.20 (Target 1). TBT also gains as 30Y approaches 5.00%. The HOLD regime is maintained and the portfolio's hawkish-regime hedges (UUP + TBT) both compound through July.
bear_case: Monday June 22 DXY opens at 99.50 as weekend risk-off subsides and Iran deal disinflation impulse accelerates; the market prices that PCE will come in soft. DXY drifts toward 99.00 through the week; on June 25 PCE prints 3.1% YoY (disinflationary surprise). DXY breaks below 99.00 — Gate 3 cleared, BUY upgrade fires. UUP falls to $26.75, stop triggered at $26.50. Simultaneously: NVDA add activates at $205–215, GOOGL entry opens, META add opens. The portfolio rotates from HOLD hedges (UUP, TBT partial) to risk-on longs. UUP is a cost that paid off by signaling the regime change.
invalidation: $26.50 daily close (DXY below 99.00, BUY upgrade); OR two consecutive DXY closes below 98.50 (risk-on acceleration, full hedge unwind); OR May PCE June 25 prints below 3.0% YoY (extreme disinflation surprise removes all Warsh justification); OR Warsh publicly signals a pause or rate path revision in a speech before June 25 (e.g., a June 22–24 Warsh speaking event that walks back the nine dots)

outcome.outcome_label: Target 1 hit at $28.20 — DXY sustained above 101 through June quarter-end
outcome.note: UUP reached $28.35 by June 22 and has held above $28.20 (Target 1) as DXY maintained 101.33 through June 29. The Warsh hawkish rate regime plus the $165B quarter-end institutional selling sustaining dollar demand delivered Target 1. DXY never closed below 99.00 (the BUY upgrade gate), confirming the thesis that the rate premium would dominate any geopolitical disinflation. Exit Target 1 at $28.20 vs $27.34 entry, +3.1%.
